$comment: US-330 / ADR-051: THE canonical allowlist of core commands that ship UNPREFIXED (no `cu-`). ADR-046 gives core assets the `cu-` emission prefix; a command escapes it ONLY by carrying `namespace: core` in its frontmatter AND appearing in `active` below. This file is the MACHINE-READABLE authority consumed by check-white-label-core.py; ADR-051 is the PROSE authority, and tests/regression/test_universal_command_allowlist.py asserts the two agree in BOTH directions , because two sources of one truth with nothing comparing them is how the epic rosters drifted for months (US-330 S2 D2). Do NOT add a slug here to silence the guard: the guard exists precisely so the bare namespace cannot grow by a frontmatter line alone. Amend ADR-051 first, then this file, in that order.
$active_comment: Commands that ship bare TODAY. `kit` predates this policy (ADR-046, via `namespace: core`) and is listed so the guard does not fail on the one command that already had the right. `memory-update` joined 2026-07-30 by maintainer decision (US-330 AC3), renamed from `cu-memory-update`. `hello`, `bye` and `session-summary` are declared here ahead of US-331/332/333 shipping them , see $reserved_comment for why that is legal.
$reserved_comment: RESERVED-FUTURE members (ADR-038; US-275 dream, US-274 distill, US-270 learn). They are named so the set is a deliberate whole rather than an accretion, and each amends `active` when its story ships. The guard checks ONE direction only , bare-but-unlisted FAILS, listed-but-not-yet-bare is LEGAL , precisely so this reserved list is expressible. `learn` carries an OPEN surface question (`learn` vs `/kit learn`) owned by US-270 at build time.
